questions.question: In April 2025, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) reduced the policy repo rate by 25 basis points, bringing it down to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**6.00%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **first bi-monthly monetary policy** review for the financial year **2025-26**, held in **April 2025**, the **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** of the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** decided to reduce the **policy repo rate**.
 
• The **MPC** implemented a reduction of **25 basis points (bps)**, which successfully brought the **repo rate** down from **6.25%** to **6.00%**. ***Hence, the correct answer is 6.00%.***
 
• The primary objective behind this rate cut is to stimulate **economic growth** by lowering the cost of borrowing for **commercial banks**, which in turn benefits **businesses** and **individual consumers**.
 
• This decision was taken by a majority vote within the **six-member committee**, assessing the prevailing **inflation** levels and the global **macroeconomic** environment.
 
• By adjusting the **repo rate**, the **RBI** manages the **liquidity** in the banking system, ensuring that **inflation** remains within the target range of **4% (+/- 2%)** while supporting **GDP growth**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Repo Rate (Repurchase Rate):**

 
 
• It is the rate at which the **Central Bank (RBI)** lends money to **commercial banks** against **government securities** to meet their short-term fund requirements.
 
• A decrease in the **repo rate** typically leads to cheaper **loans** (Home, Auto, Personal) for the general public, as **banks** pass on the benefit of lower costs to **borrowers**.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate:**
 
 
• This is the rate at which the **RBI** borrows money from **commercial banks** within the country to absorb excess **liquidity** from the market.
 
• Usually, the **reverse repo rate** is lower than the **repo rate**, creating a **corridor** for interest rate movements.
 
 
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory body established under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, specifically through an amendment in **2016**.
 
• It consists of **6 members**: **3 members** from the **RBI** (including the **Governor** as the ex-officio **Chairperson**) and **3 external members** appointed by the **Government of India**.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps):**
 
 
• In finance, **100 basis points** are equal to **1%**. Therefore, a **25 bps** cut represents a **0.25%** reduction in the interest rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Banking Sector:** When the **RBI** reduces the **repo rate**, banks often reduce the interest rates on **Fixed Deposits (FDs)** and **Savings Accounts**, which may impact the income of **senior citizens** and **savers**.
 
• **Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate:** These rates are typically adjusted in alignment with the **repo rate** changes. The **MSF** is the rate at which **banks** can borrow **overnight** from the **RBI** against their excess **SLR (Statutory Liquidity Ratio)** securities.
 
• **Stance of Policy:** The **MPC** also announces its **monetary policy stance**, such as **'accommodative'**, **'neutral'**, or **'withdrawal of accommodation'**, to signal future interest rate trajectories.
 
• **Inflation Target:** The **Government** and **RBI** have set a target for **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation to ensure price stability, which is a key factor in deciding whether to hike or cut the **repo rate**.

questions.question: In April 2025, which protected area was officially notified as India’s 107th national park?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Similipal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, the **Similipal** region in **Odisha** was officially notified as India’s **107th National Park**, marking a significant milestone in India's conservation efforts.
 
• Located in the **Mayurbhanj district** of **Odisha**, this notification provides the area with the highest level of legal protection under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972**.
 
• While the region was already recognized as a **Wildlife Sanctuary** and a **Tiger Reserve**, the status of a **National Park** ensures stricter regulations regarding human activity and habitat preservation.
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** issued the final notification following the settlement of rights and boundary demarcations by the **State Government of Odisha**.
 
• Similipal is renowned for being the only natural habitat in the world for **Melanistic Tigers** (black tigers), and this upgraded status aims to further protect their unique genetic lineage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Similipal Biosphere Reserve:**

 
 
• It was formally designated as a **Tiger Reserve** in **1956** and became part of **Project Tiger** in **1973**.
 
• It was declared a **Biosphere Reserve** by the Government of India in **June 1994** and has been part of the **UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves** since **2009**.
 
• The park derives its name from the **'Simul'** (red silk cotton) trees that are found in abundance in the region.
 
• Geographically, it features spectacular waterfalls such as **Barehipani** (one of India's highest) and **Joranda**.
 
 
 
• **National Parks in India:**
 
 
• National Parks are areas reserved for the improvement of wildlife where activities like **forestry, grazing, or cultivation** are not permitted.
 
• With the addition of Similipal, the total number of National Parks in India stands at **107** as of **2025**.
 
• The **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** empowers both the Central and State governments to declare areas as National Parks if they are of adequate ecological, faunal, floral, or geomorphological importance.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Options:**
 
 
• **Hemis National Park**: Located in **Ladakh**, it is the **largest National Park** in India and is world-famous for its **Snow Leopards**.
 
• **Bhitarkanika National Park**: Also located in **Odisha** (Kendrapara district), it is famous for its **mangrove ecosystem** and **Saltwater Crocodiles**.
 
• **Ranthambore National Park**: Located in **Sawai Madhopur, Rajasthan**, it is one of the most famous **Tiger Reserves** in Northern India, known for its diurnal tigers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Flora and Fauna:** Similipal is home to over **1,000 species of plants**, including **94 species of orchids**. Besides tigers, it supports populations of **Asian Elephants**, **Gaur** (Indian Bison), and **Chausingha** (Four-horned Antelope).
 
• **Tribal Population:** The area is inhabited by several indigenous tribes, including the **Erenga Kharias** and the **Mankirdias**, who have lived in harmony with the forest for generations.
 
• **Conservation Challenges:** The region often faces threats from **forest fires** during the summer months and **poaching**, which the National Park status aims to mitigate through increased funding and administrative surveillance.

questions.question: In the November 2025 by-elections, elections were held for the Assembly constituency in which of the following northeastern states?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Mizoram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Election Commission of India (ECI)** scheduled by-elections for several Assembly constituencies across India in **November 2025** to fill vacancies in state legislatures.
 
• In the **northeastern region** of India, the state of **Mizoram** was the primary focus for these by-polls, specifically concerning the **South Tuipui** Assembly constituency (or relevant vacant seat). ***Hence, the statement regarding Mizoram is correct.***
 
• The voting process for the **Mizoram** by-election was conducted on **November 13, 2025**, along with other states such as **Uttar Pradesh**, **Punjab**, and **Kerala**.
 
• The primary reason for conducting these by-elections was to address vacancies created by the **resignation** or **death** of the sitting **Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs)**, ensuring continued representation for the constituents.
 
• The **counting of votes** and official declaration of results for the **Mizoram** seat were finalized on **November 23, 2025**, by the **Chief Electoral Officer** of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **By-Elections (Special Elections)**:
 
 
• A **by-election** is held to fill a political office that has become vacant between regularly scheduled elections.
 
• Under **Section 151A** of the **Representation of the People Act, 1951**, the **Election Commission** is required to fill casual vacancies in the **Houses of Parliament** and **State Legislatures** within **six months** from the date of the vacancy.
 
• However, a by-election is not required if the remainder of the term of the member is **less than one year**.
 
 
 
• **Mizoram Legislative Assembly**:
 
 
• The **Mizoram Legislative Assembly** is a **unicameral** body consisting of **40 members**.
 
• The state is situated in the **northeastern** part of India, and its legislative proceedings are governed by the **Speaker**.
 
• The **Governor** of the state has the constitutional authority to summon and prorogue the sessions of the assembly under **Article 174**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Election Commission of India (ECI)**:
 
 
• The **ECI** is a constitutional body established under **Article 324** of the **Constitution of India**.
 
• It oversees the entire electoral process, including the enforcement of the **Model Code of Conduct (MCC)** to ensure free and fair polls.
 
• In the **2025 by-elections**, the commission utilized advanced **Electronic Voting Machines (EVM)** and **Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT)** systems to maintain transparency.
 
 
 
• **Geographic and Demographic Context**:
 
 
• **Mizoram** shares international borders with **Myanmar** and **Bangladesh**.
 
• Elections in this region often face unique challenges due to **hilly terrain** and **remote locations**, requiring the **ECI** to set up special polling stations for accessibility.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **November 2025 Electoral Cycle**: The **November 2025** phase was significant as it involved **48 Assembly constituencies** and **2 Parliamentary seats** across **15 states** in India.
 
• **Constitutional Mandate**: Ensuring that no constituency remains unrepresented for more than **180 days** is a core tenet of Indian **parliamentary democracy**.
 
• **Voter Participation**: In **Mizoram**, the voter turnout during by-elections typically remains high, reflecting the active political engagement of the local **tribal communities** and **civil society organizations**.
</ul

• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, through its **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, officially shifted its stance to **Neutral** by **June 2025**. This move signifies a departure from the previous "**withdrawal of accommodation**" stance that had been maintained to tackle post-pandemic inflationary pressures.
 
• A **Neutral** stance implies that the central bank is open to moving interest rates in either direction—increasing or decreasing—depending on the evolving **macroeconomic data**, particularly **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation and **GDP growth** trends.
 
• The transition away from an **Accommodative** policy began in **2022** as the **RBI** raised the **Repo Rate** to curb **Retail Inflation**. By mid-**2025**, the stabilization of inflation within the target band of **4% (+/- 2%)** prompted the shift back to **Neutral**.
 
• The **MPC**, led by the **Governor of the RBI**, evaluates various domestic and global factors before deciding on the stance. The shift to **Neutral** indicates that the **policy rates** are currently aligned with the objective of achieving the inflation target while supporting economic expansion.
 
• This policy change provides the **RBI** with greater flexibility to respond to global economic shocks or shifts in **Liquidity** conditions within the Indian banking system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Monetary Policy Stances:**
 
 
• **Accommodative Stance:** This is adopted when the **RBI** is prepared to expand the **money supply** and lower **interest rates** to boost economic growth. It was notably used during the **COVID-19 pandemic** to provide **liquidity support**.
 
• **Neutral Stance:** Under this, the **central bank** keeps its options open. It neither commits to a rate cut nor a rate hike, allowing the **Repo Rate** to be adjusted based on real-time **economic indicators**.
 
• **Hawkish Stance:** This indicates a priority to control **inflation**. The central bank is likely to increase **interest rates** to reduce the money supply and cool down an overheating economy.
 
• **Dovish Stance:** This is the opposite of Hawkish, where the focus is on low-interest rates to encourage **borrowing** and **investment**, often at the risk of higher inflation.
 
 
 
• **The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC):**
 
 
• The **MPC** is a **six-member** statutory body constituted under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934** (specifically **Section 45ZB**).
 
• It consists of **three internal members** from the **RBI** and **three external members** appointed by the **Central Government**.
 
• The committee meets at least **four times a year** (usually **bi-monthly**) to determine the **Policy Repo Rate** required to achieve the **inflation target**.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Targeting Framework:**
 
 
• The **Government of India**, in consultation with the **RBI**, sets a **flexible inflation target**. Currently, the target is **4%** with an upper tolerance limit of **6%** and a lower tolerance limit of **2%**.
 
• The primary tool used to manage this is the **Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)**, which includes the **Repo Rate** and the **Reverse Repo Rate** (or the **Standing Deposit Facility**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Repo Rate:** The rate at which the **RBI** lends money to **commercial banks** in the event of any shortfall of funds. It is used to control **inflation**.
 
• **Withdrawal of Accommodation:** A transitional stance where the **RBI** gradually removes the **excess liquidity** pumped into the system during an **Accommodative** phase.
 
• **Impact on Consumers:** A shift to a **Neutral** stance often signals a peak in the **interest rate cycle**, suggesting that **EMIs** on home and auto loans may stabilize or eventually decrease if a rate cut follows.
</ul

questions.question: Which Ministry gave the idea of a common board for class 10 and 12 in seven states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Education** (formerly known as the Ministry of Human Resource Development) has proposed the idea of a common assessment framework to bring **uniformity** across different state and central boards for **Class 10 and 12**.
 
• This initiative is primarily driven through the establishment of **PARAKH** (Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development), which acts as a **national assessment center**.
 
• The primary objective of this move by the **Ministry of Education** is to address the **disparity in evaluation** and marking schemes among various boards, which often affects students during college admissions in **Higher Education Institutions**.
 
• By proposing a common platform or "common board" guidelines for assessment, the ministry aims to ensure that **equivalence** is maintained between **State Boards**, **CBSE**, and **ICSE**.
 
• This reform was discussed in series of workshops involving representatives from various states to create a **benchmark** for student assessment that aligns with global standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Education Policy (NEP) 2020**:
 
 
• The **NEP 2020** is the foundational document that recommended the setting up of a **standard-setting body** to guide school boards on assessment patterns.
 
• It emphasizes moving away from **rote learning** and towards **competency-based assessment** for **Class 10 and 12** students.
 
 
 
• **PARAKH (National Assessment Centre)**:
 
 
• Launched in **2023**, **PARAKH** is an unit under the **NCERT** (National Council of Educational Research and Training).
 
• It is tasked with setting **norms, standards, and guidelines** for student assessment and evaluation for all recognized school boards in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Diversity of Boards**:
 
 
• India currently has more than **60 different school boards**, each following its own syllabus and grading system.
 
• The **Ministry of Education** aims to bridge the gap between these boards to provide **equal opportunities** to students from rural and urban areas regardless of their board affiliation.
 
 
 
• **Equivalence of Certification**:
 
 
• A major focus of the **Ministry of Education** is to ensure that the difficulty level of exams and the **grading rigor** are comparable across all states, preventing "grade inflation" in specific regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Focus on Seven States**: The initial phase of discussing the common assessment framework involved deep consultation with various states to pilot the **standardization** of question papers and evaluation methods.
 
• **Holistic Progress Card (HPC)**: As part of these reforms, the **Ministry of Education** introduced the **360-degree Holistic Progress Card**, which tracks a student's **cognitive, affective, and psychomotor** domains instead of just marks.
 
• **Impact on Admissions**: Standardizing **Class 12** marks is crucial because many **central universities** and competitive exams rely on board percentages for eligibility or merit ranking.
 
• **Implementation Agency**: While the idea came from the **Ministry of Education**, the technical execution is supported by **NCERT** and international assessment experts to ensure **validity and reliability** of the new system.
</ul

questions.question: In June 2025, which district was officially declared the first single-use plastic (SUP)–free district in Odisha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nuapada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the district of **Nuapada** achieved the significant milestone of being officially declared the **first single-use plastic (SUP)–free district** in the state of **Odisha**.
 
• The declaration was the culmination of a rigorous and sustained campaign led by the **District Administration** to eliminate the usage of prohibited plastic items across both **urban and rural areas**.
 
• Success was achieved through the effective implementation of the **Plastic Waste Management Rules**, which included **strict enforcement**, regular **raids on wholesalers**, and the promotion of sustainable alternatives.
 
• The initiative involved widespread **community participation**, where local **Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** and **Panchayati Raj Institutions** were empowered to monitor and report the use of **Single-Use Plastics**.
 
• To support the transition, the district set up several **Material Recovery Facilities (MRFs)** to ensure that plastic waste already in circulation was collected and processed efficiently. ***Hence, the correct answer is Nuapada.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding Single-Use Plastic (SUP):**
 
 
• **Single-use plastics** refer to plastic items that are intended to be used only **once** for the same purpose before being **disposed of** or recycled.
 
• These items, such as **plastic straws**, **stirrers**, **polythene bags**, and **plastic cutlery**, are major contributors to **environmental pollution** as they do not biodegrade.
 
 
 
• **Plastic Ban in Odisha:**
 
 
• The **Government of Odisha** has been a pioneer in environmental conservation, having initially banned plastic in **six major cities** (Bhubaneswar, Cuttack, Berhampur, Sambalpur, Rourkela, and Puri) on **Gandhi Jayanti** in **2018**.
 
• The statewide ban aligns with the **National Ban** on identified SUP items introduced by the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** which came into effect on **July 1, 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Plastic waste is a significant threat to **marine life** and **soil fertility** in **Odisha**, particularly affecting sensitive zones like **Chilika Lake** and the **Bhitarkanika Mangroves**.
 
• By becoming **SUP-free**, districts like **Nuapada** help in reducing the **carbon footprint** and preventing the clogging of **drainage systems** during the monsoon.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **District Context:** While **Nuapada** took the lead in **2025**, other districts such as **Bargarh**, **Rayagada**, and **Kalahandi** have also been actively pursuing **waste management** protocols to achieve similar status.
 
• **Legal Framework:** The enforcement is carried out under the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, where violators can face heavy **fines** or even **imprisonment** for non-compliance with plastic waste regulations.
 
• **Alternatives Promoted:** As part of the **SUP-free** movement, the government has encouraged the use of **cloth bags**, **jute products**, and leaf-based plates (**Sal leaves**), which are traditional to **Odisha's culture** and support local **artisans**.
 
• **Role of SPCB:** The **State Pollution Control Board (SPCB)** provides technical guidance and monitors the **air and water quality** improvements resulting from reduced plastic incineration and littering.

questions.question: Who is the author of 'Lords of Earth and Sea: A History of the Chola Empire', published in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anirudh Kanisetti**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The book titled **'Lords of Earth and Sea: A History of the Chola Empire'** is authored by the acclaimed historian and researcher **Anirudh Kanisetti**.
 
• Published in early **2025**, the book provides a deep dive into the **Chola dynasty**, one of the most powerful and influential empires in **South Indian** history.
 
• The narrative focuses on the **maritime prowess** of the Cholas, their sophisticated **administrative systems**, and their cultural impact that resonated across **Southeast Asia**.
 
• **Anirudh Kanisetti** is known for his ability to weave complex archaeological and epigraphic evidence into a compelling narrative for general readers.
 
• The book acts as a thematic successor to his highly successful debut work, **'Lords of the Deccan'**, which covered the history of medieval South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anirudh Kanisetti:**
 
 
• He is an **Indian historian** and researcher who has worked at various think tanks such as the **Takshashila Institution**.
 
• His first book, **'Lords of the Deccan: Southern India from the Chalukyas to the Cholas'**, was released in **2022** and won several accolades, including the **Tata Literature Live! First Book Award**.
 
• He is also well-known for his popular history podcasts, such as **'Echoes of India'** and **'Yuddha'**.
 
 
 
• **The Chola Empire:**
 
 
• The **Chola dynasty** flourished between the **9th and 13th centuries CE**, reaching its zenith under rulers like **Rajaraja Chola I** and his son **Rajendra Chola I**.
 
• They are famous for the construction of the **Brihadisvara Temple** in **Thanjavur**, which is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
 
• Their **naval expeditions** led to the conquest of territories in the **Malay Archipelago** and parts of **Sri Lanka**.
 
 
 
• **Other Authors Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Shashi Tharoor:** A prominent **Indian politician** and diplomat, he has authored numerous books such as **'An Era of Darkness'** and **'The Paradoxical Prime Minister'**.
 
• **RK Narayan:** One of India's greatest novelists, famous for his fictional town **Malgudi** and books like **'Swami and Friends'** and **'The Guide'**.
 
• **KK Aziz:** A renowned **Pakistani historian** known for his critical analysis of history textbooks and works like **'The Murder of History'**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The year **2025** marks a significant period for historical non-fiction in India with the release of this detailed monograph on the **Cholas**.
 
• The book explores the transition from regional power to **transcontinental empire**, emphasizing the **Chola navy** as a primary tool for trade and military expansion.
 
• The **Chola administration** was pioneer in **local self-governance**, as evidenced by the **Uttiramerur inscriptions** detailing village council elections.
</ul
